title: Quincy mixed-model concurrency sweep and cost projection
body:
Summary:
This note captures the April 2031 mixed-model concurrency sweep we ran for Project Quincy. Purpose: characterize latency tail (p95/p99), sustained throughput, and token-level cost when using an intelligent router that splits requests between a quantized small model (Q-7B-INT4) and a full-precision assistant model (A-70B-FP16). Goal was to find operating points that meet customer SLOs (p95 < 250ms for short prompts, p95 < 500ms for long prompts) while minimizing cost per 1M tokens.

High-level finding (TL;DR):
- Routing short requests to Q-7B with aggressive batching + warmed KV cache yields the best cost/latency tradeoff for conversational workloads dominated by short turns (<=64 tokens).
- For mixed-length workloads with ~20% long tails (>512 tokens), a hybrid policy (short->Q-7B, long->A-70B) with asynchronous fallback reduces p99 spikes and reduces cost ~38% vs always using A-70B.
- Cold starts on A-70B produce p95/p99 spikes up to 3x baseline; warmstart padding and persistent warm pools are necessary for strict SLOs.

Objective and success criteria:
- Characterize latency distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99) and throughput (req/sec, tokens/sec) for: all-Q-7B, all-A-70B, and hybrid-router.
- Produce cost model: $/1M input+output tokens (including GPU amortized cost and overhead).
- Validate that hybrid routing meets customer SLOs with <50% of baseline A-70B spend.

Test matrix (executed):
- Models: Q-7B-INT4 (quantized, lower VRAM), A-70B-FP16 (high-accuracy).
- Deployment modes: hosted-dedicated (dedicated pool of 4xA100-80GB), private-small (single 2xH100 node), hosted-shared baseline.
- Cache: KV cache disabled vs prefix warm vs persistent warmed pool.
- Batching: none, micro-batch (batch_size=8), burst-batch (batch_size=32).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 5, 20, 80, 200 concurrent in-flight requests (simulated with ramp and hold).
- Payload distributions: 80/20 short-long split (short=avg 32 tokens input, long=avg 640 tokens input).

Workload generator and measurement details:
- Used loadgen v0.9.3 (SE branch) with token-level tracing enabled.
- Each run = 10 minute steady-state after 2 minute ramp. We recorded per-request latency, token counts, KV hit/miss, batching size, and GPU utilization at 5s sample.
- Cost model: amortized GPU runtime cost measured via internal billing hook + 10% infra overhead + metadata processing cost (measured as a flat 0.6ms per request).

Representative results (selected operating points):
1) All-A-70B-FP16, dedicated pool (4xA100-80GB):
   - Concurrency 20 (steady): throughput 18 req/s (avg tokens/sec 9.6k), p50=210ms, p95=480ms, p99=820ms.
   - Cost: $420 per 1M tokens (input+output).
   - Notes: tail driven by occasional cache misses and kernel contention at >16 concurrent requests. Cold start p95 up to 1.6s.

2) All-Q-7B-INT4, private-small (2xH100):
   - Concurrency 80: throughput 75 req/s (avg tokens/sec 6.0k), p50=95ms, p95=240ms, p99=430ms.
   - Cost: $120 per 1M tokens.
   - Notes: accuracy lower on long-form (>512 tokens) completions; KV caching reduced latency by ~22% for repeat prefixes.

3) Hybrid router (short->Q-7B, long->A-70B) on dedicated pool (Q-7B colocated, A-70B in warm pool):
   - Effective concurrency 80 across router: short-path throughput 62 req/s, long-path throughput 10 req/s. Aggregate p95 (short)=180ms, p95 (long)=420ms.
   - Cost: $260 per 1M tokens (weighted). ~38% savings vs all-A-70B with similar user-visible quality for short queries.
   - Tail behavior: p99 requests primarily came from long-path A-70B coldstarts and kernel preemption during heavy background flushes.

Micro-observations and hypotheses:
- Batching helps Q-7B significantly for throughput but increases p95 for short requests if batch window >10ms. We observed a sweet spot batch delay=6ms.
- KV cache hit rate matters more for long-form continuations than for short single-turn queries. In hybrid, enabling prefix caching on Q-7B reduced overall cost by ~6% because it increased short-path success and lowered fallback to A-70B.
- GPU utilization on A-70B nodes reached 92% at 20 concurrent long prompts; small spikes in scheduler latency correlate to p99 spikes. Consider isolating long-prompt workers or fair-queueing.
- Quantization (INT4) had expected mild degradation on hallucination tests; customer acceptance tests show tolerable quality loss on short answers.

Recommendations for customer POC configuration:
1) Start with hybrid-router policy (short threshold <=64 tokens -> Q-7B) with dynamic fallback to A-70B if perplexity/confidence below threshold.
2) Configure Q-7B with micro-batching (batch_delay=6ms, max_batch=16) and persistent warmed replicas (keep-alive pool = 2 replicas) to avoid cold starts.
3) A-70B should run in a small warm pool (min_replicas=1, max_burst=2) with health checks that pre-warm KV cache for known prefixes where possible.
4) Enable token-level tracing and cost attribution for 2 weeks in production trial to validate model routing decisions.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Omar: spin up hybrid test on customer staging and enable trace-level sampling (due 2031-04-15).
- Priya: add accuracy pass comparing Q-7B vs A-70B for 1200 customer-specific prompt samples and submit results (due 2031-04-17).
- Jasper: implement warm-pool autoresize policy in serving runtime prototype PR #987 (linked) and run one end-to-end load (due 2031-04-20).
- Rina (me): consolidate cost model into customer-facing one-pager and schedule workshop with product & infra (due 2031-04-19).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: customer has regulatory requirement forcing all inference on high-accuracy model. Mitigation: evaluate quantization-aware fine-tuning to reduce accuracy gap or use A-70B-only with autoscaling and cost projection.
- Risk: unpredictable long-form spikes will drive p99 > SLO. Mitigation: implement circuit-breaker that routes high-latency requests to degraded-but-fast model for non-critical paths.

Appendix A — raw numbers (condensed):
- All-A-70B (conc20): p50=210ms, p90=340ms, p95=480ms, p99=820ms, throughput=18 req/s, tokens/sec=9600, cost=420 $/1M tokens.
- All-Q-7B (conc80): p50=95ms, p90=200ms, p95=240ms, p99=430ms, throughput=75 req/s, tokens/sec=6000, cost=120 $/1M tokens.
- Hybrid (conc80, 80/20 split): short-path p95=180ms, long-path p95=420ms, agg tokens/sec=8300, cost=260 $/1M tokens.

Appendix B — experiment notes:
- Several runs had noisy network artifact between 2031-04-11 14:22-14:30 UTC; those minutes were discarded.
- We used a synthetic user arrival pattern that approximates customer telemetry (bursty morning peak, steady tail).

Open questions for customer workshop:
- Acceptable accuracy threshold for routing decisions (metric we should use: BLEU/ROUGE/Truthfulness score?).
- Will customer accept partial fallbacks for non-critical UI elements?
- Data residency constraints for private deployment vs hosted (affects where Q-7B can be colocated).

Notes-to-self:
- Capture a short demo video showing router behavior under burst and coldstart scenarios.
- Add a follow-up run to exercise 95/5 short-long split and 50/50 split to see sensitivity.

-- end of note --
